name: Monasterio de San Juan de los Reyes

position.source: https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/21282452 (centroid of the outline, in the cloister garden; the north wall of the church runs along the long axis 63.3°/243.3°)

rights.note: Founded 1477 by the Catholic Monarchs; church and cloister by Juan Guas (master builder 1479–1496, with the sculptor Egas Cueman), finished after his death by Enrique and Antón Egas (church 1495, cloister c. 1504–1510); the north portal designed by Alonso de Covarrubias (1553), finished 1610. Burnt in 1808; restored by Arturo Mélida from 1883 and again after 1940.

notes: Built by code (model_sources/Q1289106_san_juan_de_los_reyes.py, tools/meshkit.py) with AI assistance. The church: single nave of four bays (granite, 23.3 m to the cornice) with pointed windows, the cresting along their sills and along the roofline, buttresses with pinnacles and statues, the chapels between the south buttresses under the cloister roof, a hipped tiled roof; the head (23.6 m) with its balustrade, corner pinnacles, the great north window, the blind arcades, the frieze and the iron chains of the captives on its north and east faces; the octagonal lantern over the crossing with its windows, corner pinnacles, balustrade, ribbed dome, little lantern and cross (38.3 m); the north portal (Covarrubias) with clustered pilasters, statues, niche, gable and cross, on the Plaza de San Juan de los Reyes (y = 0, ground_at); the west door at the level of the street below the west end, and the stair turret on the north-west corner. The cloister: two floors of arcades on the garden (pointed arches with tracery below, mixtilinear arches over balustrades above, piers with pinnacles, cresting), the walks with their floor, vault and lean-to roofs; the garden in four hedged beds round the well, with a fir, a magnolia and two orange trees (not mapped: placed as on the photographs). The convent ranges (rendered, tiled roofs) from the OSM parts. Every wall goes down to 1.5 m below the real ground (MDT05). Uncertain: the heights of the lantern and the dome (±2 m), the west portal (its design and the level of its sill; the street there is about 5 m below the plaza), the heights of the ranges (from their levels in OSM), the trees. The brief named the Covarrubias portal as the west one: it is on the north side, facing the plaza (photographs), and is modelled there. Simplified: tracery, sculpture and heraldry, the interior.
